summary: MaintHelp is an ASP.NET web page and code module supporting the maintenance and editing of help records within an HSPnet system. It provides a user interface for listing, searching, filtering, viewing, editing, adding, deleting, and previewing help content tied to specific screens or modules. The page leverages update panels, modal popups, validation controls, grid and detail views, and integrations with the backend data layer to manage help records.
purpose: The purpose of MaintHelp is to provide system administrators and maintainers with a dedicated interface for managing help documentation related to various screens in HSPnet. This includes creating, updating, and deleting help text and titles, as well as previewing and searching for help records, ensuring users have accurate and context-sensitive assistance.

workflows.name: View Help Records
steps: Page loads and initializes user session.
Default listing of help records displayed in GridView (gridData).
User can filter records by entering a keyword (txtKeyword) or selecting a starting character (lbStartsWith_Click).
GridView is refreshed with filtered results.

workflows.name: Add Help Record
steps: User clicks 'Add' button (cmdAdd or cmdAddEmptyData).
Switches DetailsView to add mode.
User enters ScreenName, HelpTitle, HelpText, HelpTitleAlt, HelpTextAlt.
Required field validators ensure mandatory values.
User clicks 'Save' (cmdSave).
New HelpRecord is created and added to backend via UserSession.

workflows.name: Edit Help Record
steps: User clicks 'Edit' button in GridView.
DetailsView switches to edit mode with fields populated.
ScreenName cannot be edited; label is shown, textbox hidden.
User modifies fields and clicks 'Save'.
Record is updated in backend and GridView refreshed.

workflows.name: Delete Help Record
steps: User clicks 'Delete' button.
Confirmation required.
HelpRecord is deleted via UserSession.
GridView is refreshed.

workflows.name: Preview Help Record
steps: User clicks 'Preview' button.
JavaScript opens help screen in new window with session information.
Display preview of help content.

business_rules: ScreenName is required for all help records.
HelpTitle and HelpText fields are mandatory.
HelpTitleAlt and HelpTextAlt are mandatory when alternate locale is used.
GridView and DetailsView use validation controls to enforce mandatory fields.
validations: RequiredFieldValidator for ScreenName, HelpTitle, HelpTitleAlt, HelpText, HelpTextAlt.
ValidationSummary displays list of errors when fields are missing or invalid.
Client-side and server-side validations ensure correct inputs.
calculations: Truncate HelpText and HelpTextAlt for GridView display to 75 characters.
conditions: If ScreenName is empty (new record), textbox is shown for entry.
If editing existing record, ScreenName is displayed as label and cannot be modified.
If keyword is empty, default search uses '%' to fetch all records.
system_behavior: Uses AJAX UpdatePanel for partial page updates and responsive UI.
Modal popups used for editing and validation without full page reload.
AlwaysVisibleControlExtender keeps error and warning panels visible.
Handles error and warning messages centrally via dedicated panels.
dependencies: HSPnet.DataLayer.Help for data retrieval and modification.
HSPnet.UI.Grid for client scripting and utility functions.
AjaxControlToolkit for modal popups and always visible controls.
Resource files for localization of labels, tooltips, and error messages.
exceptions: Error panel displays when backend operation fails (e.g., save, delete).
Warning panel shown for status messages or non-critical issues.
ValidationSummary shows errors if required fields are missing.
content_gaps: Business rules for alternate locales and help text specifics are inferred from field validators and requirements; actual locale logic and help text processing not shown.
No example help records or sample data present.
Limited detail on error handling logic and specific exceptions.
No explicit permission or user role validation shown; assumed System Administrator or Maintainer access.
